title: Buffer anchor tester
blurb: Interactive RegExp tester with u/v/m/g/i flag toggles, multiline presets, a zero-width caret character strip, and the TC39 explainer's 9-row truth table for /\Afoo|^bar$|baz\z/um.
question: Do \A, \z, and \Z in Unicode mode (u/v) stay anchored to buffer boundaries even with the m flag enabled, matching all nine rows of the TC39 proposal truth table?
result: Verified in Chrome 153 headless: flag-off throws SyntaxError ('Invalid escape'); with --js-flags=--js-regexp-buffer-boundaries or --enable-features=V8Flag_js_regexp_buffer_boundaries, all 9 README truth-table rows and 10/10 conformance assertions pass. Default-on Chrome 160 without flags not yet verified.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 (default and --js-flags=--js-regexp-buffer-boundaries); not verified flag-free in Chrome 160

friction.summary: No chrome://flags switch enables buffer boundaries before Chrome 160, and --enable-experimental-web-platform-features / --js-flags=--harmony do not turn it on
friction.repro: Launch Chrome 153 with --enable-experimental-web-platform-features or --js-flags=--harmony and run new RegExp('\\A', 'u'); it still throws SyntaxError: Invalid escape.
friction.workaround: Pass --js-flags=--js-regexp-buffer-boundaries or --enable-features=V8Flag_js_regexp_buffer_boundaries on pre-160 builds, or feature-detect via try { new RegExp('\\A', 'u'); }.
